candidates.original_title: RAF inhibitors prime wild-type RAF to activate the MAPK pathway and enhance growth
candidates.description: Replicates the original claim that RAF inhibitors paradoxically activate MEK/ERK signaling in BRAF[WT] cancer cell lines, as measured by IC50 values across a panel of cancer cell lines (Figure 1A)
candidates.citation_sentence: Hatzivassiliou and colleagues found that RAF inhibitors, while effective in blocking signaling in BRAF[V600E] mutant (MT) cancer cell lines, paradoxically increased cell proliferation in BRAF[WT] cancer cell lines (Hatzivassiliou et al., 2010).
candidates.notes: Paper is a registered report protocol paper from the Reproducibility Project: Cancer Biology; results are not reported in the provided text. [ling26: extra entry, not in the external record]

candidates.original_title: RAF inhibitors prime wild-type RAF to activate the MAPK pathway and enhance growth
candidates.description: The original study claimed that BRAF[V600E]-mutant cancer cell lines are sensitive to RAF inhibitors, whereas BRAF[WT] cell lines, including RAS-mutant and RAS/RAF-wild-type lines, are not; this claim was tested in Protocol 1.
candidates.citation_sentence: Hatzivassiliou and colleagues found that, while drugs targeting CRAF were able to inhibit CRAF activity in vitro, they paradoxically increased cell proliferation in BRAF[WT] cancer cell lines (Hatzivassiliou et al., 2010).
candidates.notes: This is a registered replication report describing a planned experiment; no replication outcome is reported, so the result is inconclusive. [luna56: extra entry, not in the external record]

candidates.original_title: RAF inhibitors prime wild-type RAF to activate the MAPK pathway and enhance growth
candidates.description: The original study claimed that silencing CRAF reverses RAF-inhibitor-induced MEK activation in KRAS-mutant HCT116 cells; this claim was tested in Protocol 2.
candidates.citation_sentence: Hatzivassiliou and colleagues found that, while drugs targeting CRAF were able to inhibit CRAF activity in vitro, they paradoxically increased cell proliferation in BRAF[WT] cancer cell lines (Hatzivassiliou et al., 2010). As reported in Figure 2B, silencing CRAF reversed MEK activation upon treatment with the RAF inhibitors GDC-0879 and PLX4720.
candidates.notes: This is a registered replication report describing a planned experiment; no replication outcome is reported, so the result is inconclusive. [luna56: extra entry, not in the external record]

candidates.original_title: RAF inhibitors prime wild-type RAF to activate the MAPK pathway and enhance growth
candidates.description: The original study claimed that the CRAF-BRAF kinase-domain heterodimer is destabilized by PLX4720 and stabilized by GDC-0879; this claim was tested in Protocol 3.
candidates.citation_sentence: Hatzivassiliou and colleagues found that, while drugs targeting CRAF were able to inhibit CRAF activity in vitro, they paradoxically increased cell proliferation in BRAF[WT] cancer cell lines (Hatzivassiliou et al., 2010). In Figure 4A, Hatzivassiliou and colleagues reported that the CRAF kinase domain forms a stable complex with the BRAF kinase domain when inhibitors are not present.
candidates.notes: This entry covers the single heterodimerization claim tested with multiple inhibitor conditions. This is a registered replication report describing a planned experiment; no replication outcome is reported, so the result is inconclusive. [luna56: extra entry, not in the external record]
